source_caption:
A Guide for the Married Man is a comedy starring Walter Matthau. It follows a happily married man whose friend tries to convince him to start having affairs, giving him a so-called “guide” on how to cheat without getting caught.

The film plays out as a series of humorous scenarios and fantasies, showing both the temptations and the complications of infidelity. While it leans into comedy, it also ends up highlighting the value of loyalty and the risks of trying to outsmart relationships.

source_details.synopsis: A Guide for the Married Man is a 1967 American bedroom-farce comedy film directed by Gene Kelly and starring Walter Matthau, Inger Stevens, and Robert Morse. It features many cameos, including those by Lucille Ball, Jack Benny, Terry-Thomas, Jayne Mansfield, Sid Caesar, Carl Reiner, Joey Bishop, Art Carney, and Wally Cox. The title song, performed by the Turtles, was composed by John Williams, with lyrics by Leslie Bricusse.
